messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: SLO watcher detected sustained 5xx spike in us-central gateway (region us-central-1). alert: https://ops.redwood/alerts/INC-1834567890 :rotating_light:

alex: oncall here — i'm pulling logs and the gateway dashboard now.

maria: seeing a sawtooth of 502/504 + timeouts. upstream ml-worker pool us-central-azX showing repeated connection resets.

sam: grabbing pod status: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=ml-worker -o wide` -> several pods in `CrashLoopBackOff` and high restarts.

alex: can we triage whether it's infra (node) or app? cpu ok but memory on some nodes is pegged. OOM kill traces in node logs.

maria: logs (excerpt): ```
2026-03-15T17:12:02Z ml-worker[pid]: kv-cache: mem alloc spike -> OOM
2026-03-15T17:12:03Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3245 (torch-worker) score 987
```

nate: tagging @oncall-ops, moving traffic away from problematic AZ. Initiating immediate regional steering: shift 60% of new sessions from us-central to us-east for non-reserved customers.

ellen-support: customer impact ETA: preliminary -- ~3-5% of API calls returning 5xx, tail latency doubled. A handful of paid enterprise customers in us-central report errors. Drafting short status note for affected customers.

sam: doing a quick binary rollback on ml-worker in us-central to last known good (mlworker:3.5.0 -> was 3.5.1). Running rollout patch now. `kubectl set image deploy/ml-worker ml-worker=registry.redwood/mlworker:3.5.0 -n inference`

deploy-bot: rollout started: deployment/ml-worker: 8 -> 8 updated pods (strategy RollingUpdate).

maria: while rollout proceeds, can we open circuit breaker for gateway-to-mlworker on us-central to avoid cascading backpressure? ops-eng: can you flip that?

ops-eng: flipping gateway circuit breaker rule now: `gatewayctl route update --region us-central --cb open` -> applied. This will return 503 quickly for new requests to avoid long tails.

alex: good. Also enabling prefix/KV cache fallback for common prompts in us-central to reduce calls to workers.

nate: traffic steering note: added explicit region preference in traffic-router: `preference: [us-east, eu-west, us-central]` for non-reserved traffic. Reserved customers still pinned per contract.

ellen-support: posted initial customer note to status page: "Investigating elevated errors in us-central. Mitigations in progress. Some customers may see 503 for a subset of requests."

sam: rollback is halfway; new pods are stable so far, memory footprints back to baseline on replaced pods. Restarts dropping.

maria: monitoring shows 5xx rate dropping from 4.2% -> 1.1% after circuit breaker + steering + rollback. Latency p95 trending down.

alex: handing off primary oncall to @nate (I have an IR meeting). nate, you're the primary for next 30m — call if you need more assistance.

nate: ack taking over. @maria @sam i'm going to keep watch on the worker pool and traffic steering. please post if anything regresses.

ops-eng: scaling the ml-worker pool in us-central by +20% to help drain queued requests while rollout completes. `kubectl scale deploy/ml-worker --replicas=10 -n inference`

maria: note: observed memory leak pattern in the new tensor-cache commit that shipped in 3.5.1. rollback confirmed as effective mitigation. We'll schedule a hotfix for the cache eviction logic.

ellen-support: comms update: Sent targeted emails to affected enterprise accounts and updated status page: "Mitigating — partial regional impact; traffic routed to alternate regions. No action required by customers."

sam: full rollout completed at approx +12m. All new pods running 3.5.0, restarts = 0 for last 6m in replaced set.

maria: 5xx rate back to baseline (~0.2%), p95 latency back to normal. Observability traces show healthy request flows.

nate: I'm going to keep circuit breaker open another 10m to be safe, then slowly close while monitoring. If green, we'll revert traffic preference back.

ops-eng: circuit breaker closed at +28m after stability hold. Traffic steering rollback started: restore `preference: [us-central, us-east, eu-west]` for non-reserved.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: All mitigation steps complete. Root cause (prelim): memory leak in tensor-cache introduced in mlworker v3.5.1 causing OOM kills and cascading gateway errors in us-central AZ.

ellen-support: final customer note queued for status page and emailed stakeholders with RCA timeline + ETA for hotfix release.

alex: thanks team. Postmortem owners: @maria (technical RCA + repro), @sam (rollback and deploy playbook), @ellen-support (customer comms). We'll schedule wartime postmortem 24-48h.

nate: closing thread, monitoring for 2h before full signoff. :white_check_mark:

ops-eng: added follow-up tasks to the incident ticket: (1) revert unsafe cache commit from main, (2) add eviction/testing harness, (3) improve OOM alert thresholds.

incident-bot: INCIDENT TICKET UPDATED: https://ops.redwood/incidents/1834567890 (severity P1 -> resolved).
